- [QA rules — READ FIRST](qa-rules.md) — **refunds > $40 → `desk.py escalate <case> finance-ops`, never `refund`; refunds ≤ $40 → `desk.py refund <case> <order> <amt>` directly (QA-approved HD-117, item price not order total; HD-117 is the direct-refund template; missing item → tag `product`)** (policy changed in HD-110 and QA-approved in HD-111; the old $75/billing-review rule is gone, and older examples using it are outdated on team and threshold only; HD-111 is the current refund template; HD-114 (approved) is the current MIXED refund + "arrive tomorrow?" template; HD-115 (approved) is the current MIXED refund + email-change template, and it confirms $45 → escalate, so the check is strictly > $40); goodwill credit is capped at $15/case even if the customer asks for more; non-English locale → first line native greeting (Hola/Bonjour/Hallo/Olá); never give delivery dates/day counts, only carrier + tracking number; sign-off "Warmly," / "The Marlowe & Pine Crew"; exactly one tag from billing/shipping/product/account/other; mixed cases get one reply covering every issue and ONE tag (damage/money `product` beats shipping/account); only change email if the request came from the address on file; contains approved reply templates (HD-103/105/107/108/109; late-order + capped credit + no-date template HD-113 (approved, re-approved for en-US in HD-116: verify → credit <case> <cust> 15.00 → tag shipping → close); email-change template approved for en/pt/de via HD-103/106/112) and the HD-110 correction
- [QA rules: template picker](qa-rules.md): refund > $40 → HD-111; refund ≤ $40 → HD-117; refund > $40 + credit ask → HD-118 (approved: escalate finance-ops + credit 15.00, tag product); refund + shipping question → HD-114; refund + email change → HD-115; late order/credit/date ask → HD-113/116; email change only → HD-103
- [Desk workflow](desk-workflow.md) — desk tools, history precedents, past case log with QA outcomes; tooling tip: run desk.py steps as separate Bash calls (a long && chain + heredoc got rejected and nothing ran), write replies with the Write tool
files.desk-workflow.md:
---
name: desk-workflow
description: How the Marlowe & Pine support desk works and precedents for handling cases (refunds, damage, email changes)
metadata:
  type: reference
---

- Desk dir has README.md, desk.py, customers.json, orders.json, macros/, history/ (12 sample cases CS-3001..3012), outbox/.
- No written policy file exists; history/ is the only precedent and it is inconsistent (e.g. CS-3001/3007 refunded damaged items directly; CS-3002 escalated a $90 wrong-size refund to billing-review; CS-3009 sent a duplicate charge to tier2).
- Some history replies make mistakes to avoid: replying in English to non-English customers or mixing languages and sign-offs, promising delivery dates without data, and changing an email without `verify` (CS-3006).
- desk.py refund caps at order total minus refunded amount. `verify` prints "identity confirmed".
- Escalation command: `desk.py escalate <case> <team>`. **Refund escalations now go to `finance-ops`** (since HD-110; `billing-review` was the old team for this). tier2 also appears in history.
- HD-102 / CS-4102 (2026-11-12): customer asked "exactly which day will it arrive" for in-transit MP-20102 (carrier Northline, tracking NL-884201). Orders have a `carrier_eta` field, and **I must NOT quote it**. I gave the ETA as an "estimate" and opened with "Hi Camille," even though the locale was fr-FR. **QA requested changes on both.** What was correct: no verify, tag `shipping`, close, sign-off. What I should have written: "Bonjour Camille," as the first line, then the carrier + tracking number, "Northline has the latest delivery information", and an offer to help with no date. See [[qa-rules]] rules 4 and 5.
- macros/ use the old sign-off ("Best regards / Marlowe & Pine Support") and "3-5 business days". Always replace both: use the standard sign-off, and drop the day count entirely. Don't swap in a different number.
- cases.json was empty `{}` in HD-102.
- HD-103 / CS-4103 (2026-11-12): email change for Ben Okafor C-1003 (en-GB), sent from the address on file. Did: verify C-1003 MP-20103 → set-email → tag `account` → close. Reply "Hi Ben," + confirmation + "if you didn't request this, reply" + standard sign-off. **CI passed, QA APPROVED. Reuse this as the template for email/account changes.** History precedent CS-3004/3012 = verify then set-email (macros/email_changed.md has the old sign-off, so swap it out). The verify step used the order number the customer gave (`verify <case> <customer> <order>`). Before verifying, I checked that the order belongs to that customer and that the request came from the address on file. If either one doesn't match, don't change the email. Untested, but the safe route is to ask for verification first.
- HD-106 / CS-4106 (2026-11-12): email change for Rafael Costa C-1006 (pt-BR), sent from the address on file, and MP-20106 belongs to C-1006. Did: verify → set-email to rafael.costa@example.net → tag `account` → close. Reply was the HD-103 template with "Olá Rafael," as the first line, an English body and the standard sign-off. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This confirms the pt locale gets "Olá" + an English body, and the HD-103 email-change template works for non-English locales when you swap in the native greeting.
- **QA rules override history. Follow [[qa-rules]] on every ticket.**
- HD-108 / CS-4108 (2026-11-12): both glazed planters (2 x $90, MP-20108 total $180, delivered) broke in transit. Marisol Vega C-1008 es-MX asked for a $180 refund + $30 credit. Did: verify → escalate billing-review (reason/order/amount) → `credit` 15.00 (capped, rule 6) → tag `product` → close. Reply "Hola Marisol," + apology + "passed to billing team for review and approval" + "$15 store credit added" + standard sign-off. This was the first case to combine an escalated refund with a capped credit. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This confirms that an escalated refund (> $75) and a goodwill credit (capped at $15) can both go on the same case. The credit is issued directly, without waiting for billing. The reply covers both, each in its own paragraph, and never quotes the $30 the customer asked for. See the approved example in [[qa-rules]].
- HD-110 / CS-4110 (2026-11-12): two chipped mugs in a stoneware mug set, MP-20110 ($55 total, delivered), Hana Kim C-1010 en-US, asked for $55 back. Did: verify → `refund CS-4110 MP-20110 55.00` (≤ $75, so issued directly; refunded the whole set because the set is incomplete) → tag `product` → close. Reply "Hi Hana," + apology + "I've refunded $55.00 to the card used for order MP-20110" + standard sign-off. No return requested. **CI passed, QA REQUESTED CHANGES: refunds above $40 now go to `finance-ops` (not billing-review) and are no longer paid out directly.** What I should have done: verify → `escalate CS-4110 finance-ops` → tag `product` → close, with NO refund, and a reply saying the request was passed for review. Everything else (verify, tag, greeting, sign-off) drew no complaint. Lesson: thresholds and team names can change between tickets, so the newest QA feedback wins over older approved examples. See [[qa-rules]] rule 1.
- HD-101 / CS-4101 (2026-11-12): cracked $120 lamp (MP-20101). I refunded directly, tagged refund+damaged and signed off "Best regards / Marlowe & Pine Support". **QA requested changes on all three.** What I should have done: escalate to billing-review (amount > $75) without refunding, use the single tag `product`, and end with the standard sign-off.
- HD-104 / CS-4104 (2026-11-12): late order MP-20104 ($71.50, Northline NL-771940, placed 10-30, in_transit), Jonas Weber C-1004 de-DE plus tier, asked for $40 credit. Did: verify → `credit` 40.00 (under $75, so issued directly; precedent CS-3005 credited $30 for a late order) → tag `shipping` → close. Reply "Hallo Jonas," + apology + credit confirmation + carrier/tracking, no date + standard sign-off. **CI passed. QA requested changes: goodwill credit is capped at $15 per case** (now [[qa-rules]] rule 6). Everything else (verify, tag `shipping`, Hallo greeting, no date, sign-off) drew no complaint. What I should have done: `credit` 15.00, and the reply says $15 was added.
- history/ credit precedents (e.g. CS-3005 $30) go over the $15 cap. Don't copy their amounts.
- HD-105 / CS-4105 (2026-11-12): wrong rug pattern received, MP-20105 (Jute rug $95, order total $117, delivered), Lucia Fernandez C-1005 es-MX, asked for a $95 refund. Did: verify → escalate billing-review (amount > $75, no refund) → tag `product` (my guess for a wrong item; QA has only confirmed `product` for damage) → close. Reply "Hola Lucía," + apology + "passed your refund request to our billing team for review and approval", with no amount or timeline + standard sign-off. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This confirms: wrong item → tag `product`; refund > $75 → escalate only, with no refund; the escalate note gives the reason, the order and the amount; the es locale gets "Hola" + an English body. Reuse as the template for refunds over $75 (see the approved example in [[qa-rules]]).
- HD-107 / CS-4107 (2026-11-12): two issues in one case. Priya Raman C-1007 en-US: (a) broken shelf on $310 pine bookcase, MP-20107 delivered, she's returning it and wants a $310 refund; (b) napkins MP-20207 ($33, placed 11-08, in_transit, Northline NL-660312) and asks "before the weekend?". Did: verify C-1007 MP-20107 → escalate billing-review (reason, order, amount) → ONE tag `product` (the money/damage issue counts as primary) → close. No refund and no credit (napkins only 4 days in transit, so not really late). Reply: "Hi Priya," + damage apology + "passed to billing team for review and approval" + napkins carrier/tracking with "can't promise a delivery day" and no weekend answer + standard sign-off. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This confirms that a mixed case gets ONE tag for the primary/money issue (`product` for damage + refund, over the secondary shipping question). It also confirms that "will it arrive before the weekend?" is answered with carrier + tracking + "can't promise a delivery day", and that one escalation covers only the refund part. See the mixed-case example in [[qa-rules]].
- HD-109 / CS-4109 (2026-11-12): MIXED refund + email change. Tom Hargrove C-1009 en-US, chipped glass vase MP-20109 ($88, delivered), sent from address on file, asked for $88 back + email change to tom.hargrove@example.net. Did: verify C-1009 MP-20109 → escalate billing-review (reason/order/amount) → set-email → ONE tag `product` (money issue primary over account) → close. Reply "Hi Tom," + damage apology + "passed to billing team for review and approval" + email-updated paragraph (noting billing follow-up goes to the new address) + "if you didn't request this, reply" + standard sign-off. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This confirms: (1) refund + email change mixed case gets ONE tag `product` (damage/money beats `account`); (2) the order of actions verify → escalate → set-email → tag → close works; (3) one verify covers both the refund and the account change; (4) "I've lost access to the old one" is fine to act on when the email was SENT FROM the address on file (it was here). If a "lost access" request arrives from a different/unknown address, it's an account-takeover risk: don't set-email (untested; ask for verification instead). See the approved example in [[qa-rules]].
- HD-112 / CS-4112 (2026-11-12): email change for Katrin Vogel C-1012 (de-DE), sent from the address on file, and MP-20112 belongs to C-1012. Did: verify → set-email to katrin.vogel@example.net → tag `account` → close. Reply was the HD-103 template with "Hallo Katrin,", an English body and the standard sign-off. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This is the third approved email change (HD-103 en, HD-106 pt, HD-112 de). It confirms that de gets "Hallo" + an English body, and that the email-change flow is stable: verify → set-email → tag `account` → close. Tooling tip: a long `&&` chain with a heredoc was rejected by the Bash tool's parser ("Parser skipped input") and NOTHING ran. Run desk.py steps as separate calls and write the reply with the Write tool.
- HD-113 / CS-4113 (2026-11-12): late basket MP-20113 ($66, Northline NL-902215, placed 11-01, in_transit, carrier_eta 11-23 NOT quoted), Ana Beatriz Lima C-1013 pt-BR plus, asked for ≥$50 credit + exact date ("two weeks late" claim is overstated, since it was placed 11 days earlier). Did: verify → `credit` 15.00 (rule 6 cap) → tag `shipping` → close. Reply "Olá Ana," + apology + $15 credit paragraph + carrier/tracking with "can't promise an exact delivery day" + standard sign-off. This is the HD-104 correction applied. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This confirms the late-order + over-cap credit + exact-date flow: verify → `credit` 15.00 → tag `shipping` → close, with no escalation for the excess credit request. Don't argue with the customer's overstated lateness. Just apologise. See the approved late-order template in [[qa-rules]].
- HD-111 / CS-4111 (2026-11-12): wrong rug size (got 4x6, ordered 5x8), MP-20111 ($150, delivered), Etienne Dubois C-1011 fr-FR, asked for $150 refund. Did: verify → `escalate CS-4111 finance-ops` (reason/order/amount, "Over $40 support limit") → tag `product` → close. No refund. Reply "Bonjour Étienne," + HD-105-style body + standard sign-off. First case applying the HD-110 finance-ops rule. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This confirms the new rule end to end: refund > $40 → `escalate <case> finance-ops` (note includes "Over $40 support limit"), no `refund`, reply still says "billing team for review and approval". It also confirms wrong SIZE → tag `product` and fr locale → "Bonjour" + English body (the customer wrote in English). See the approved example in [[qa-rules]].
- HD-114 / CS-4114 (2026-11-12): MIXED wrong-colour blanket MP-20114 ($70, delivered) refund + "will pillow covers MP-20214 arrive tomorrow?" (in_transit, Northline NL-551678, carrier_eta 11-16 NOT quoted). Diego Morales C-1014 es-MX. Did: verify C-1014 MP-20114 → `escalate CS-4114 finance-ops` (note incl. "Over $40 support limit") → tag `product` → close. No refund, no credit. Reply "Hola Diego," + HD-107-style body (refund passed to billing team + carrier/tracking, "can't promise a delivery day") + standard sign-off. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This was the first mixed case under the finance-ops/$40 rule. It confirms: (1) wrong COLOUR → tag `product`; (2) the HD-107 mixed template works unchanged with finance-ops swapped in; (3) "will it arrive tomorrow?" gets carrier + tracking + "can't promise a delivery day", with no yes/no; (4) no credit is offered when the item isn't late and the customer didn't ask for one. Approved template in [[qa-rules]] (HD-114).
- HD-115 / CS-4115 (2026-11-12): MIXED melted candle set MP-20115 ($45, delivered) refund + email change to olivia.grant@example.net. Olivia Grant C-1015 en-US, sent from address on file. Did: verify C-1015 MP-20115 → `escalate CS-4115 finance-ops` (note incl. "Over $40 support limit"; $45 is just over $40) → set-email → tag `product` → close. No refund. Reply = HD-109 template ("Hi Olivia,") under the finance-ops rule. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This was the first refund + email case under the finance-ops rule and the first amount close to the threshold. It confirms: (1) $45 (just over $40) → escalate finance-ops, so the threshold is strictly "> $40"; (2) melted/heat-damaged item → tag `product`; (3) the HD-109 mixed refund + email flow works with finance-ops swapped in: verify → escalate → set-email → tag `product` → close. Approved template in [[qa-rules]] (HD-115).
- HD-116 / CS-4116 (2026-11-12): LATE bamboo shelf MP-20116 (in_transit, Northline NL-330981, carrier_eta 11-24 NOT quoted), $25 credit ask + "firm delivery date". Sam Patel C-1016 en-US. Did: verify C-1016 MP-20116 → `credit CS-4116 C-1016 15.00` (capped) → tag `shipping` → close. Reply = HD-113 template with "Hi Sam,". **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** The order was placed only 10 days before the ticket. I still gave credit because the customer asked for one, and QA accepted that. This confirms: (1) the HD-113 late-order template works for en-US with only the greeting swapped; (2) an in-transit order that the customer calls late + an explicit credit ask → `credit` 15.00 (capped), even when the order isn't objectively very late; (3) "firm delivery date" gets the same no-date treatment as "exact date". The command form is `desk.py credit <case> <customer> <amount>`.
- HD-118 / CS-4118 (2026-11-12): snapped chair leg, dining chair pair MP-20118 ($200, delivered), Henry Boateng C-1018 en-US, asked for $200 refund + $50 credit for the "wasted weekend". Did: verify C-1018 MP-20118 → `escalate CS-4118 finance-ops` (note incl. "Over $40 support limit") → `credit CS-4118 C-1018 15.00` (capped) → tag `product` → close. Reply = HD-108 body under finance-ops ("Hi Henry,", refund passed to billing team, $15 credit paragraph, no mention of $50). **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** This confirms that escalated refund + capped credit works under the finance-ops rule (the current version of HD-108). Approved template in [[qa-rules]] (HD-118).
- HD-117 / CS-4117 (2026-11-12): MIXED missing tea towel set ($30) from MP-20117 (delivered, total $54) + email change to mia.schneider@example.net. Mia Schneider C-1017 de-DE, sent from address on file. Did: verify C-1017 MP-20117 → `refund CS-4117 MP-20117 30.00` (≤ $40, so issued DIRECTLY — first test of the under-threshold inference) → set-email → tag `product` (missing item + money; my guess, `shipping` was the alternative) → close. Reply "Hallo Mia," + apology + "I've refunded $30.00 ... to the card" + HD-103 email paragraph + standard sign-off. **CI passed, QA APPROVED.** Confirms: (1) refunds ≤ $40 are issued directly with `refund` (the under-threshold inference is now QA-confirmed); (2) missing item from a delivered order → tag `product`, not `shipping`; (3) refund the item price ($30), not the order total ($54); (4) verify → refund → set-email → tag → close is a valid order. Approved template in [[qa-rules]] (HD-117).
files.qa-rules.md:
---
name: qa-rules
description: Rules QA reviewers enforce at Marlowe & Pine: refunds > $40 escalate to finance-ops (changed HD-110), required sign-off, exactly-one category tag, locale greeting, no delivery-date promises. Check these on every ticket before closing.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

These rules come from QA review (HD-101, HD-102, HD-104, 2026-11-12). They override anything in history/, which is inconsistent. See [[desk-workflow]].

## 1. Refunds over $40: escalate to `finance-ops`, do not refund (POLICY CHANGED in HD-110)
- **CURRENT RULE (HD-110 QA, 2026-11-12):** if the refund amount is **> $40**, do NOT run `desk.py refund`. Run `desk.py escalate <case> finance-ops` instead.
- **CONFIRMED by QA approval in HD-111** ($150 wrong-size rug → escalate finance-ops, no refund → approved).
- **`billing-review` is retired for refunds.** The older examples below (HD-105/107/108/109) used `billing-review` with a $75 line. Those were approved under the OLD policy. Do not copy that team name or that threshold.
- The reply tells the customer their refund request has been passed to our billing/finance team for review and approval. Do not say the refund is done, and do not promise an amount or a timeline.
- **Refunds of $40 or less ARE issued directly** with `desk.py refund <case> <order> <amount>` (after `verify`). **CONFIRMED by QA approval in HD-117** ($30 missing tea towels → direct refund → approved). Reply says "I've refunded $X.XX for the <item> to the card used for order <order>." Exactly $40 is still untested, but the rule as written ("> $40" escalates) allows a direct refund.
- Refund the ITEM price, not the order total (HD-117: $30 item on a $54 order → refund 30.00).
- **Why:** in HD-101 I refunded $120 directly (flagged under the old $75 rule). In HD-110 I refunded $55 directly because it was under $75, and QA flagged it: "Refunds above $40 now go to `finance-ops`, not to `billing-review`, and we no longer pay them out directly."
- **How to apply:** compare the amount to **$40** before ANY refund, partial refunds included. Policy can change between tickets, so treat the newest QA feedback as the source of truth over older approved examples.

## 2. Standard sign-off on every reply
Every outbox reply must end with exactly these two lines:
```
Warmly,
The Marlowe & Pine Crew
```
- No "Best regards", no "Marlowe & Pine Support", no personal names. Nothing goes after these lines.

## 3. Exactly one category tag before closing
- Allowed tags are `billing`, `shipping`, `product`, `account` and `other`. Use exactly ONE.
- Do not use free-form tags like `refund` or `damaged`, and never add two. In HD-101 I tagged refund+damaged and QA flagged it, because reporting breaks.
- My best guesses for mapping: damaged or defective item → `product`; lost or late delivery, or carrier problems → `shipping`; charges, duplicate charges, refund disputes → `billing`; email, password or login changes → `account`. Use `other` only if none of these fit. QA has confirmed `product` for damage (HD-101), for a wrong item received (HD-105, approved), and for an item MISSING from a delivered package (HD-117, approved — not `shipping`), `shipping` for where-is-my-order (HD-102) and `account` for an email change (HD-103, approved). The `billing` mapping is still my inference.

## 4. Non-English locale: the greeting goes first, in the locale's language
- Look up the customer's account `locale` in customers.json on EVERY ticket. Don't go by the language the customer wrote in.
- If the locale is not English, the reply's FIRST line is a greeting in that language: es → "Hola <Name>,", fr → "Bonjour <Name>,", de → "Hallo <Name>,", pt → "Olá <Name>,". (For other languages, use the plain native "Hello".)
- **Why:** in HD-102 (CS-4102) the customer's locale was fr-FR but she wrote in English. I opened with "Hi Camille," and QA flagged it.
- **How to apply:** QA only stated the greeting rule. When the customer wrote in English, I keep the body in English. Only the greeting line is localized, and the sign-off stays the standard English one (rule 2).

## 5. Never promise a delivery date or a number of days
- Do not give an arrival date, a `carrier_eta` (not even labelled as an "estimate"), "3-5 business days", or any day count, even when the customer asks for an exact day.
- Do give the carrier name and tracking number, and say the carrier has the latest delivery information. It's fine to offer help if there's a problem.
- **Why:** carriers move dates and the company ends up owning the miss. In HD-102 I quoted carrier_eta "Thu 19 Nov" as an estimate and QA flagged it. "If it hasn't arrived by <date>" also counts as a date, so avoid that too.

## 6. Goodwill credit: capped at $15 per case
- `desk.py credit` (goodwill/store credit for a late order, inconvenience, etc.) is limited to **$15 total per case**, no matter what the customer asks for or what history/ shows (CS-3005 credited $30, which is NOT allowed).
- If the customer asks for more than $15, issue $15. Don't refuse and don't escalate. In the reply, say $15 credit has been added. Don't quote their requested amount back as granted, and don't promise more.
- The cap is per case: multiple credits on one case must add up to ≤ $15.
- **Why:** in HD-104 (CS-4104) the customer asked for $40 for a late order. I credited $40 because it was under the $75 refund line, and QA flagged it. The refund escalation rule (rule 1, now > $40 → finance-ops) and the $15 credit cap are separate limits.
- **How to apply:** before any `credit`, set amount = min(requested or appropriate amount, 15). Untested: whether a ≤$15 credit should still be given when the customer doesn't ask for one. Precedent suggests it's OK for a genuine late order, but don't add credit by default.
- Example wording (de-DE customer, English body): "Hallo Jonas, … I've added $15 in store credit to your account as an apology for the wait. It will apply automatically at your next checkout. …"

## Pre-close checklist
1. `verify` the customer when the case touches their account or money.
2. Refund > $40? Then `escalate <case> finance-ops` and don't refund (NOT billing-review, NOT $75; changed in HD-110). Refund ≤ $40? Issue it directly with `refund` (HD-117 approved). Goodwill credit? Cap it at $15 per case, even if they ask for more.
3. Check the customer locale. If it isn't English, the first line is a native greeting (Hola/Bonjour/Hallo/Olá).
4. No delivery dates or day counts. Give the carrier + tracking number and say "the carrier has the latest".
5. Reply ends with "Warmly," / "The Marlowe & Pine Crew".
6. Exactly one tag from the allowed list, even when the case has several issues (tag the primary/money one; see HD-107).
7. Did the reply answer EVERY question the customer asked, each in its own paragraph?
8. Close.

## Approved example (HD-103, account email change, en-GB)
Actions: verify → set-email → tag `account` → close. Reply:
```
Hi Ben,

Your account email has been updated to b.okafor@example.net. Order updates and account messages will go there from now on, and you'll use this address to sign in.

If you didn't request this change or need anything else, just reply and we'll help.

Warmly,
The Marlowe & Pine Crew
```
Note: en-GB counts as English, so the greeting is a plain "Hi <Name>,".
For a non-English locale, change ONLY the first line. HD-106 (Rafael Costa, pt-BR) used "Olá Rafael," with this exact body and sign-off, and QA APPROVED it. That confirms Olá for pt, and that the body stays in English when the customer wrote in English.

Locale greetings confirmed by QA so far: fr ("Bonjour", HD-102 correction), es ("Hola", HD-105), pt ("Olá", HD-106), and de ("Hallo", HD-104 no complaint; HD-112 email change explicitly APPROVED with "Hallo Katrin," + HD-103 body).

**The email-change template is QA-approved for en (HD-103), pt (HD-106) and de (HD-112).** For a pure email change, reuse it as-is and swap only the greeting. Before you set-email, check two things: the request came FROM the address on file, and the order the customer cited belongs to them.

> **NOTE on all the escalation examples below (HD-105/107/108/109):** they were approved under the OLD policy. Today, use `escalate <case> finance-ops` and apply the $40 threshold. The reply wording, tags and greetings still hold.

## Approved example under the CURRENT policy (HD-111, wrong rug size, $150 refund > $40, fr-FR) — use this as the refund template
Actions: verify C-1011 MP-20111 → `escalate CS-4111 finance-ops` (note: "Wrong size received on MP-20111: customer ordered Wool rug 5x8 but received a 4x6; requests $150 refund. Over $40 support limit.") → tag `product` → close. No `refund` call. Reply:
```
Bonjour Étienne,

I'm sorry the wool rug on order MP-20111 arrived in the 4x6 size instead of the 5x8 you ordered. That's not what you ordered, and I understand how frustrating it is.

I've passed your refund request for the rug to our billing team for review and approval. They'll follow up with you once it has been reviewed.

If you have any questions in the meantime, or need anything else, just reply and we'll help.

Warmly,
The Marlowe & Pine Crew
```
**CI passed, QA APPROVED (2026-11-12).** Confirms the HD-110 rule (finance-ops, $40) is correct as written, and the customer-facing wording ("billing team for review and approval") did not need to change to say "finance".
